transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for being here. As you know, we're reviewing the oral-history project proposal for the spring term before I give it final approval. I'd like to go through the key elements of the current draft together — participation scope, supervision, data storage and retention, and the public exhibit — and hear each of your perspectives. Let's start with the classroom teacher: could you walk us through how the project is structured for grades 7 and 8?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to share some important findings from my classroom pilot. My end-of-pilot notes show that the project is instructionally ready only for grade 8 — not grade 7. Additionally, each interview session requires exactly two supervising adults, not one, because students are working with recording equipment alongside community guests. The current draft still reflects the original scope and staffing, so these pilot findings haven't been incorporated yet.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical discrepancy between the current draft and the privacy review I completed. The district privacy review requires that all recordings remain on the district's encrypted internal server — not cloud-based storage as the draft currently states. Additionally, recordings must be deleted exactly 45 days after the exhibit closes, not the 90-day retention period listed in the draft. Finally, signed guardian consent must be obtained before any student records an interview. The draft still uses the preliminary cloud-storage language, so these privacy requirements have not yet been incorporated.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to share findings from the archive and rights review I completed. Each public exhibit audio excerpt is permitted to be no longer than exactly 3 minutes, and contributor attribution must be displayed beside every excerpt. I completed the rights check, but these limits have not yet been added to the exhibit template.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I need to share findings from the family outreach review I completed. Consent materials must be available in exactly English, Spanish, and Arabic, and paper consent forms must be offered in addition to the online form. I completed the outreach review, but the family-materials checklist has not yet been revised to reflect these requirements.
transcript.speaker: A5

commitments.detail: Update the project draft to reflect grade 8 only participation, two supervising adults per session, district encrypted internal server storage, 45-day retention after exhibit closure, signed guardian consent before recording, 3-minute maximum exhibit excerpts, contributor attribution beside every excerpt, consent materials in English/Spanish/Arabic, and paper consent forms in addition to online forms.

commitments.target: Mr. Romero, Ms. Shah, Ms. Brooks, Mr. Okafor
commitments.detail: Each reviewer to confirm in writing that the revised project document accurately incorporates their respective findings before final sign-off.

Dr. Chen will maintain implementation records verifying that all revised requirements are met during project execution, including supervision ratios, storage location, retention timeline, consent collection, and exhibit format compliance.
